first_lines: Part II Nonlinear packet calculus, obstruction complexes, and holon-
This part moves from exact coordinates for arbitrary functions to differentiable interactions, specified
correction problems, and finite or smooth transport. Each ordinary proof retains its stated hypotheses.
These results are not asserted to belong to the finite Lean contract of Part I.
A vanishing linear obstruction is only the first step. We give a contraction theorem for nonlinear cor-
rection, followed by a local Lyapunov Schmidt reduction. In a complete filtered problem, every lifting
step has its own cokernel class. Vanishing at all depths and compatible choices of corrections produce
an exact inverse limit solution. A filtered correction complex carries a spectral sequence. Its first page
records graded obstruction candidates, while later differentials record interactions that can cancel them.
